subject: Discovery recap & proposed integration pathway — FinBus PoC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@finbus.com>; Aaron Lee <aaron@finbus.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed integration pathway — FinBus PoC

Hi Olivia / Aaron —

Thanks again for the meeting this morning. Below is a compact recap of what we heard, the goals you set, and a pragmatic integration path for a 3-week PoC. I copied Grace (solutions) and Priyom (CS) to own the technical and success items.

What you described (primary pain points)
- Latency spikes during peak batch runs for invoice parsing and reranking (~300–400ms target currently missing).
- High per-token cost at scale with current provider; looking for predictable unit economics.
- Data residency and auditability requirements for downstream regulators.

Current stack and constraints
- Backend: Node.js microservices on AWS EKS (K8s).
- Preprocessing: custom tokenizer + light NER pipeline in Python for entity extraction.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for single-document reranking; throughput bursts up to 200 req/s.
- Security: SOC 2 needed; potential desire for Private deployment in EU for some clients later.

Success criteria for the PoC (what 'good' looks like)
- Functional: 1) API-compatible generation + reranking integration with minimal code changes, 2) deterministic output for a set of 50 replay prompts.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 350ms for 95% of calls on your baseline traffic profile.
- Cost: projected per-1M-token unit cost at least 20% lower than current provider under PoC config.
- Compliance: demonstrated audit logs and key management integration for sample dataset.

Proposed PoC scope & milestones (3 weeks)
- Week 0 (pre-work, this week): exchange credentials, sample dataset (anonymized), and requirements doc. Owner: Aaron/Olivia to share; Jordan to coordinate.
- Week 1 (integration): Grace will provide SDK examples (Node + Python), a Dockerized runtime shim, and a reference integration to replace current API calls. Goal: end-to-end inference with sample dataset. Owner: Grace.
- Week 2 (performance tuning): runner tests, batching and cache config, measuring latency/throughput under your traffic profile. Owner: Grace + FinBus eng.
- Week 3 (validation & handoff): qualitative checks (50 prompt replay), cost modeling, compliance artifacts (audit log sample). Priyom to prepare success checklist & go/no-go criteria.

Open questions (need answers to scope accurately)
1) Can you share a white-listed set of endpoints and a sample anonymized dataset by Wed 2026-06-09?
2) Do you have existing key management preferences (AWS KMS or customer HSM)?
3) Which SDK language should we prioritize for a first-pass example (Node vs Python)?

Immediate next steps
- Olivia/Aaron: send the sample dataset + internal PoC approvers list (Aaron?) — target: Wed 2026-06-09.
- Grace: will prepare Node + Python SDK snippets and a quick-start Docker image by Fri 2026-06-11.
- Priyom: will draft a one-page success checklist and a procurement-ready term sheet (attached: redwood-poc-terms-v1.pdf).
- Jordan: schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive (links below).

Suggested times for the tech deep-dive (please confirm a single slot)
- Thu 2026-06-10 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu 2026-06-10 14:00–15:00 PT

Links / attachments
- PoC terms draft: redwood-poc-terms-v1.pdf (attached)
- Scheduling: https://cal.com/jordan-blake/finbus-tech-deep-dive

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Olivia Park <olivia@finbus.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed integration pathway — FinBus PoC

Jordan —

Thanks for the detailed recap, that aligns well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Priority: reducing cost per token is the top commercial priority, but we also cannot accept regressions in accuracy for our reranker. We will evaluate on both metrics.
- Data residency: for the initial PoC it's fine to use hosted if audit logs and retention controls are available; longer-term some clients will require EU-only processing. Please flag whether a Private (VPC) option is straightforward to enable for the PoC or if that adds significant setup time.
- Compliance: we need SOC 2 evidence and an outline of what logs are generated and retained.

I've attached our product requirements doc for context (FinBus-Roadmap-Reqs.pdf). Also can you provide a ballpark monthly cost estimate for the PoC configuration (approx traffic: 5M tokens/month during test) so I can clear internal budget?

We can commit to sending an anonymized sample dataset by Wed 2026-06-09.

Thanks —
Olivia
Head of Product, FinBus Inc.
olivia@finbus.com | +1 (646) 555-0199

Attachment: FinBus-Roadmap-Reqs.pdf

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed integration pathway — FinBus PoC

Thanks, Jordan and Olivia — quick note from the solutions side:

- I'll prepare two repo branches: node-integration-example and python-integration-example. Each will include a small shim that maps your existing request/response shapes to Redwood's API, plus a Dockerfile you can run in your CI.
- I'll also produce a benchmarking harness (simple k6 script + token calculator) so we can reproduce latency/throughput and estimate cost under your 5M tokens/month profile.
- Regarding Private/VPC: we can demo a VPC-connected control plane for audit logs; full on-prem air-gapped setup typically adds ~3–4 weeks. For the PoC, VPC connectivity is feasible if you can provide network owners for the brief setup.

Action items from my side:
- Node + Python examples and Docker image: target Fri 2026-06-11
- Benchmark harness + initial cost estimate: target Mon 2026-06-14
- I'll push a short checklist of what I need from FinBus (sample endpoints, baseline qps, any blocked IP ranges).

Also attaching the procurement term draft to Jordan for review so procurement has something to start with.

Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
